LESSON: POLITE LANGUAGE

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Polite language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Polite language
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we use polite language?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use euphemisms to show politeness
2. identify short forms in oral literature
3. speak politely in public

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ What is a euphemism?

• A euphemism is a soft / polite way of saying something that might sound harsh or embarrassing.
• We use euphemisms to show respect and good manners.

▸ Euphemism for politeness

Teach
• Think of the direct word.
• Replace it with a kinder phrase.
• Keep the meaning, soften the sound.

Worked example
• Direct: “He died.” → Polite: “He passed away.”
• Direct: “She is old.” → Polite: “She is advanced in age.” / “She is elderly.”
• Direct: “The toilet” in formal talk → Polite: “the washroom” / “the restroom”.
• Direct: “You failed.” → Polite: “You did not meet the mark this time.”

Try this
• Change to polite language: “Your breath smells.”
• Change to polite language: “That man is jobless.”
• (Check later: e.g. “Your breath is not fresh.”; “He is between jobs / seeking employment.”)

▸ Short forms in oral literature (examples)

• Riddles — short clever questions for entertainment and thinking.
• Proverbs — short wise sayings.
• Tongue twisters — short phrases for clear speech practice.

Worked examples
• Proverb idea: “A stitch in time saves nine.” → Fix a small problem early.
• Polite classroom talk: “Please may I borrow your pen?” not “Give me your pen.”


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings
• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 direct sentences, then rewrite each with a euphemism / polite form.
2. Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
3. Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Collect 5 euphemisms from home/radio/news. Write direct + polite pairs.
2. Prepare a 1-minute polite speech thanking visitors at school.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we use polite language?
2. Why is it embarrassing to say some words in public?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
